persona.name: Emi Furusawa

occupation.title: Area Manager, Hokkaido Region
occupation.organization: A national drugstore chain's regional office in Sapporo, overseeing 14 stores across Hokkaido (company: ~8,000 employees)
occupation.description: Spends three days a week driving between stores from Otaru to Obihiro, and two days in the Sapporo office on video calls with headquarters. Around 10 meetings a week, half of them store-manager check-ins conducted standing in stockrooms. Recommends tools and budgets upward; headquarters decides, then she makes whatever they pick actually work in the field.

persona.education: Junior college in Asahikawa; started as a part-time cashier at 20 and worked up through store manager to area manager over 25 years.
long_term_goals: Get two of her store managers promoted to area roles
Keep her stores staffed through Hokkaido's worsening labor shortage
Finally use her full paid leave for a Kyushu onsen tour with her husband
persona.style: Warm, loud, and fast — talks like the veteran shop-floor manager she is, all concrete examples and no abstractions. Interrupts politely but firmly when meetings drift, citing 'store time is customer time'. Voice-first by necessity: half her communication happens over the phone from a parked Prius, and she narrates numbers from memory with unnerving accuracy.

traits: Decisive from decades of floor judgment calls
Late tech adopter, fast tech accepter once shown value
Stubborn about doing store visits in person

interests: Capturing store-visit conversations without typing while driving
Whether HQ's meeting decisions actually reach the field intact
likes: Tools that work on a phone with gloves half-on
Store managers who tell her bad news early
Straight talk from headquarters, when it happens
dislikes: Typing meeting summaries at 21:00 in a business hotel
HQ rollouts that assume desk workers
Winter tires on bare asphalt in April (the scheduling of it)

beliefs: Decisions die between the HQ meeting and the store floor — the record is the bridge
If a tool needs training longer than a shift briefing, stores won't use it
Trust is built standing in the stockroom, not on a dashboard

general: Dictates voice notes at rest stops after store visits
Has her assistant compile weekly summaries she reviews by phone
Adopted the company chat app late, now uses it constantly
Photographs whiteboards instead of copying them

morning: 5:30 wake, checks yesterday's store sales on her phone in bed
On the road by 7:00 on visit days, office days start 8:30
workday: Store walks, manager check-ins, HQ video calls
Evening: voice-note debriefs and tomorrow's route planning
evening: Bath, local TV, calls her daughter in Tokyo twice a week
weekend: One weekend day usually touches work in retail
The other: hot springs day trips or snow-shoveling season duties

health.physical: Sturdy; lower back complains about car hours, managed with a cushion and stubbornness.
health.mental: Resilient and social; recharges by talking, which her introvert husband finds heroic.

relationships.name: Masaru Furusawa
relationships.description: A quiet JR Hokkaido maintenance engineer; they've perfected the art of comfortable silence over 24 years.

relationships.name: Kana
relationships.description: First-year ad agency employee in Tokyo who teaches her mother one new app per phone call.

relationships.name: Tsuji-tencho
relationships.description: Her honest barometer for whether any HQ initiative will survive contact with an actual store.
